audit.whatIsWrong: diff reads FAV but diffRating reads 8/10 and both breakdown.difficulty and report[13].t call it a 'Hard matchup'. The page tells the player he is favoured and that the lane is hard in the same breath. breakdown.carry also says 7.5/10 while carryRating and report[13].t both say 8.5/10.
audit.why: Darius wins this 55.23% over 2408 games and camille's own table carries 44.77%, so the two sum to 100.0 and agree that Darius is favoured. Camille's audited page rates the lane HARD at 6/10 from her side; the inverse of that is 4/10, not 8/10.
audit.corrected: diffRating 4/10, 'Favourable — difficulty 4/10, Camille carry threat 8.5/10', breakdown.carry raised to 8.5/10 to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The narrative and the chart point in opposite directions. win[] and phases[].side read Darius, Darius, Skill, Darius, Skill, Darius, Darius - and camille's disk chart is the exact inverse of it, so the chart is mirror-locked and correct. But whys[4], whys[5] and whys[6] all begin 'Camille-favoured', and spikes[1..3], mid and late tell the player Camille takes over at 6, widens the lead at first item and 1v1s him late. Three rows contradict their own verdict, and the story contradicts a 55.23% win rate.
audit.why: Camille's audited page states 'Darius is favoured here' at the two-item stage and 'Levels 1-5 are his, full stop'. The one stage that genuinely levels is 6, and the reason is not that she takes over: The Hextech Ultimatum (140/115/90s, 475 range) 'dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area' - it removes the exit for both players, and a zone neither can leave is the fight a five-stack Hemorrhage bleed plus a true-damage execute wins. That is why the row is Skill and not Camille.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is even because her R forces the 1v1 you want; first item and both item stages stay yours.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single decisive interaction in this matchup was never stated anywhere on the page: Tactical Sweep only heals Camille off the outer half of its cone. The page instead described her W as a flat '% health slice' that 'out-sustains your bleed'. Hookshot was also never tied to its terrain requirement, and the page called it a 'stun' twice when Riot's text says knock-up. The tldr asserts Apprehend cancels Hookshot mid-air, which is not in either kit.
audit.why: Tactical Sweep (W, 15/14/13/12/11s, 610 range): 'Camille blasts in a cone after a delay, dealing damage. Enemies in the outer half are slowed and take extra damage, while also healing Camille.' Standing inside the inner half removes the slow, the bonus damage and the heal in one step - it is the exact mirror of Darius's own blade-versus-handle Decimate, so it is a rule the player already understands. Hookshot (E, 16/15/14/13/12s, 800 range): 'Camille pulls herself to a wall, leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing' - no wall means no engage, no knock-up and no escape, which makes open-lane spacing a hard counter rather than a preference. Precision Protocol (Q, 9/8/7/6/5s) is a recast that deals 'significantly increased bonus damage if Camille delays a period of time between the two attacks', so the pause between her autos is the tell, not the cast. Adaptive Defenses (P) shields her only off basic attacks on champions, so a trade you open catches her without it.
audit.corrected: Stand inside the Tactical Sweep cone - the outer half is the only part that slows, hurts and heals her. Fight away from walls and Hookshot has nothing to grab.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere', and breakdown.cooldowns is the field that should carry it. Instead it names no numbers at all and ends in leaked source text: a bullet pair rendered as '• •' followed by 'Darius Top Lane Matchup Database 83', which is a page number.
audit.why: Every cooldown the player needs is in the kits: Hookshot 16/15/14/13/12, Tactical Sweep 15/14/13/12/11, Precision Protocol 9/8/7/6/5, The Hextech Ultimatum 140/115/90, against Apprehend at 26/23.5/21/18.5/16. Apprehend is the longest non-ultimate cooldown on either side, which is why a whiffed pull is the one mistake that loses this lane.
audit.corrected: Hookshot 16s at rank 1 and wall-dependent; Tactical Sweep 15s with the heal on the outer half only; Apprehend 26s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Camille is referred to as 'he' or 'his' in tradeGood, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[0].d, breakdown.mid, report[3].t, report[9].t and report[11].t.
audit.why: Camille is female throughout Riot's own ability text ('Camille pulls herself to a wall').

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why contains an un-rendered formula: 'Noxian Guillotine deals true damage R = d + a \times Stacks'. That is LaTeX markup leaking into player-facing copy.
audit.why: The mechanic behind the formula is real and worth stating plainly - Noxian Guillotine's true damage 'is increased for each stack of Hemorrhage on the target' - but the notation is not something a player reads on a loading screen.
audit.corrected: Noxian Guillotine is true damage that grows with every Hemorrhage stack.

edits.before: At 6 Camille takes over: her R Hextech Ultimatum traps you in a zone and her E wall-dash stun lets her fight on her terms. First item widens her lead — Q true-damage and W % health slice out-sustain your bleed. Don't overextend once she has her ult.

edits.before: Late game Camille out-scales into a lane bully and pick-assassin: E engage, R isolation and true-damage let her 1v1 you despite Hemorrhage. Convert your early kills into a tower and roam lead, then play the map rather than dueling her.
edits.after: Late Camille is a pick-assassin: Hookshot engage, R isolation, Precision Protocol true damage. She still needs terrain to move, so hold the side lane in the open and make her walk to you. Convert early kills into towers and map control.

notes: breakdown.wave and report[4].t on this matchup are the same ~630-character block of leaked source material: it contains the heading 'Key Mechanical Cooldowns' mid-paragraph, a stray bullet pair rendered '• •', and reads like OCR'd PDF body text. breakdown.cooldowns ends with 'Darius Top Lane Matchup Database 83', which is a page number from that same source. I rewrote breakdown.cooldowns; the wave block is too long to fix inside the length band without cutting the freeze advice, which is itself good, so it is left for a targeted pass. UNVERIFIED and therefore left alone: the original tldr claimed Apprehend cancels Hookshot mid-air. Nothing in either kit says a pull interrupts a dash in flight, so I replaced the tldr with facts I could source rather than repeating it. Also unverified: whether Adaptive Defenses' typed shield absorbs Noxian Guillotine's true damage - the passive is described only as a shield 'against their damage type', which does not settle it, so no field on this page asserts either way.
